warning.bounce: Your hard-bounce rate ({rate}) in the rolling last 24 hours is approaching the limit. New broadcasts are being sent at a reduced rate until it recovers.
warning.complaint: Your complaint rate ({rate}) in the rolling last 24 hours is approaching the limit. New broadcasts are being sent at a reduced rate until it recovers.

paused.bounce: New API, batch and broadcast sends are paused due to hard bounces: {count} events across {sent} sends ({rate}) in the rolling last 24 hours. Review the list and suppressions. See the criteria and recovery steps in metrics.
paused.complaint: New API, batch and broadcast sends are paused due to complaints: {count} events across {sent} sends ({rate}) in the rolling last 24 hours. Review contact sources and consent. See the criteria and recovery steps in metrics.

recovery.title: Sending protection and recovery
recovery.pauseWindow: The pause uses the rolling last 24 hours. This window is separate from the range selected in the charts.
recovery.warningWindow: Warning and pause use the same rolling 24-hour window, independent of the chart range. Internal MepMail policy, not AWS limits.
recovery.pauseEvidence: {metric}: {count} events across {sent} sends ({rate}), in the rolling last 24 hours.
recovery.warningEvidence: {metric}: a rate of {rate} in the rolling last 24 hours in UTC, at warning level.
recovery.criteriaVolume: With at least one confirmed send in the rolling last 24 hours, either condition pauses new sends. The statistical warning floor does not exempt low-volume senders. Internal MepMail policy, not AWS limits:
recovery.bounceCriteria: At least {count} hard bounces and a rate strictly above {rate}.
recovery.complaintCriteria: At least {count} complaints and a rate strictly above {rate}.

steps.list: Fix the list at its source: remove invalid addresses and stop retrying recipients with permanent rejections.
steps.suppressions: Review the actual suppression list. Hard bounces and complaints received from the provider automatically suppress the address. Preserve these entries; removing them to retry keeps the problem in place.
steps.consent: Review contact sources, consent and segmentation. Remove people who did not authorize messages or unsubscribed from campaigns.

recovery.reevaluationAt: Estimated next evaluation: {date} UTC, if no new sends or events occur. Release depends on a fresh evaluation of the criteria; this time does not guarantee sending will resume.
recovery.reevaluationPending: The next evaluation uses current counters. The 24-hour window advances continuously. Without enough daily detail, there is no estimated improvement date yet.
recovery.automatic: Protection is reevaluated against the rolling window. Falling below a threshold does not release held mail, resume a suspended account or send a queue. Other safety controls and a warning can still apply.

sendGuard.bounce: New API, batch and broadcast sends are paused due to hard bounces. Displayed rate: {rate} in the rolling last 24 hours; protection threshold: {limit}. Review the rejected addresses. The evaluation uses the rolling last 24 hours. Other safety controls still apply; this does not release held mail or resume a suspended account.
sendGuard.complaint: New API, batch and broadcast sends are paused due to complaints. Displayed rate: {rate} in the rolling last 24 hours; protection threshold: {limit}. Review contact sources and consent. The evaluation uses the rolling last 24 hours. Other safety controls still apply; this does not release held mail or resume a suspended account.
sendGuard.regionPaused: Broadcasts are paused for a short while to protect delivery. Transactional email is unaffected, and broadcasts resume on their own. Try again later.
sendGuard.suspended: This team is suspended by the instance operator. Sending is disabled until it is reinstated.
sendGuard.operatorPaused: Broadcasts are paused for this team by the instance operator. Transactional email is unaffected.
sendGuard.regionHeld: Broadcasts are paused in {region} by the instance operator. Transactional email is unaffected. Try again later.
sendGuard.tooLarge: This audience needs more than {days} days of sending capacity. Split it into smaller segments or contact support.
sendGuard.tooLargeSelfHost: This audience needs more than {days} days of sending capacity. Split it into smaller segments or ask your instance operator for more capacity.
